new.n: Jesse Scholl's pot of gold in the basement wall, Sixth and Grand, Milwaukee (1915)
new.pl: Old Scholl homestead, 142 Sixth St (old numbering) at Sixth and Grand (now N 6th St and W Wisconsin Ave), on Sixth between Sycamore (Michigan) and Spring (Grand) as in 1858; lot not read on a Sanborn
new.v: A pot of gold coins dated 1843-61, at least $1,000-2,000; a rumoured second pot of $19,000 never produced
new.st: On 25 May 1915 labourers of the Milwaukee Wrecking Co., razing the old Scholl homestead at Sixth and Grand (142 Sixth St), struck a pot of gold with a pick near the basement wall and scattered it. The company said about $80 was left when the foreman arrived but believed 'not less than $2,000' was taken; one workman carried about $650 toward Chicago and Canada, and six others got money. The family (Jesse Scholl, 1810-1886, built the house) thought over $1,000 was in the pot and that he hid gold in the walls. A rumour of a diagram to a second pot of $19,000 brought guards and a probe of the fireplace at 146 Sixth St, with the company and the owner disputing title. Pin is the block, not the spot.
new.t: Recovered and dispersed on the spot; the $19,000 pot is a labourers' rumour the company scoffed at. Downtown block long rebuilt: look-only.
pinev: W side of Sixth between old Spring St (Grand, now Wisconsin Ave) and Sycamore (Michigan), per the 1858 directory and the 1915 'Sixth and Grand'; 142 Sixth St not yet fixed on the 1910 Sanborn, so r150 on the block.
new.tovw: Lead grade F (treasure thread): found and dispersed 1915; second pot only a rumour

tw-mi-escanaba-koster-1900s.t: The 5 Feb 1909 wire (Bay City Times, p. 1) calls him Gustave Koster of Garden; the death index has Nickolas Koester, Fairbanks Twp, 3 Feb 1909: same fire, same man.
